Priya (CSM): Heads up — Amberleaf QBR prep kickoff. Need: short account health pulse, onboarding blockers, token econ snapshot, and a recommended cost action plan. Meeting Thu 11am PT. Who can own cost + ops slide?

Ben (Sales): I'll coordinate with CFO. Renewal target date is 2026-09-12. They called out unpredictable daily spend as main blocker for renewal.

Carlos (FinOps): I can own the cost slide. Will produce: 90d burn, 30d spike table, and a 12-week forecast with three scenarios. Any large one-off jobs we should exclude?

Eve (Solutions): Amberleaf has a nightly vectorization job that runs at 03:00 UTC — that job caused two quota breaches last month. I have the job manifest and can show a quick fix: stagger shards + enable prefix caching.

Priya (CSM): Nice. Please include estimated $ savings for the fix. We want an explicit ask: either reserved capacity or daily spend cap + alerts.

ingest-bot: ingest: uploaded amberleaf-onboarding-tickets.csv to /exports/ingest/4891234567.csv

Carlos (FinOps): Uploaded forecast + anonymized chart: https://files.redwood/amberleaf/4891234567/forecast.png. Key note: the nocturnal vector job accounts for ~28% of weekly tokens on peak days. Proposed mitigations: 1) cache embeddings with TTL=7d 2) quantize model used for batch to int8 3) leveled rate-limits for pipeline steps.

Eve (Solutions): Sample snippet for caching middleware to show in QBR:

```
# caching middleware (python)
if request.type == "embed":
  key = sha256(request.payload)
  v = cache.get(key)
  if v: return v
  v = call_embed_model(request)
  cache.set(key, v, ttl=604800)  # 7d
  return v
```

Priya (CSM): Perfect. Also add a slide with onboarding feedback: most tickets flagged "unclear defaults" and "no starter configs". I'll propose a "starter kit": default batching, cache TTL, and quota guardrails.

Ben (Sales): CFO wants to see p99 latency SLA for Dedicated vs Hosted and a sample reserved quote. Can we include a quick table?

Carlos (FinOps): I'll add the cost delta table: Hosted vs Dedicated (3 commit levels). Also include a suggested temporary credit line if they choose Dedicated and need time to optimize.

Eve (Solutions): On the demo side, I'll prepare a short before/after: run their nightly job in staging (no-cache vs with-cache) and capture tokens/sec and average cost. Command I'll use:

```
# reproduce in staging
curl -X POST https://staging.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $STAGING" \
 -d '{"model":"rw-embed-2b","inputs":[...],"batch_size":128}'
```

Priya (CSM): Owners and deadlines: Carlos = cost + forecast + chart by Tue 2pm; Eve = demo + code snippet + perf numbers by Wed 9am; Ben = renewal asks and CFO notes by Tue EOD. I'll compile onboarding feedback + starter kit by Wed noon. Dry run Thu 10:15.

Ben (Sales): Quick Q: can we set an automatic spend alert at 80% daily of their configured cap? If so, include it as a near-term win.

Carlos (FinOps): Yes — we support tiered alerts. I'll include JSON for the alert rule and recommended thresholds.

Eve (Solutions): One risk: if they move to Dedicated, some of our automated cache layers may be disabled depending on their network setup. Will call that out as a tradeoff.

Priya (CSM): Great callout. Include a short mitigation note (hybrid cache or local Redis with replicate-to-redwood for cold starts).

ingest-bot: notify: ticket #AM-2145 updated with "starter kit" checklist

Priya (CSM): Thanks all — will ping Tue morning for status. :sparkles:
